title: Compatible quotient sections from projective adic targets
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $E,M$ be $R$-modules, and $v:E\to M$ a surjective $R$-linear map. For $L=E,M$ and $n\ge1$, let $I^nL$ be the submodule generated by $rx$ with $r\in I^n$, $x\in L$, put $A_n=R/I^n$ and $L_n=L/I^nL$ with its natural $A_n$-module structure, and let $q_n^L:L_{n+1}\to L_n$ be reduction. Let $v_n:E_n\to M_n$ be $[e]\mapsto[v(e)]$. Assume $M_n$ is projective over $A_n$ for every $n\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For every $n\ge1$ and every $A_n$-linear section $s_n:M_n\to E_n$ of $v_n$, there is an $A_{n+1}$-linear section $s_{n+1}:M_{n+1}\to E_{n+1}$ of $v_{n+1}$ such that $q_n^E\circ s_{n+1}=s_n\circ q_n^M$. In particular, there exists a family $(s_n)_{n\ge1}$ of $A_n$-linear maps such that $v_n\circ s_n=\mathrm{id}_{M_n}$ and $q_n^E\circ s_{n+1}=s_n\circ q_n^M$ for every $n\ge1$; the compatibility equations are equations of $R$-linear maps.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, proof: initial splitting, the induction with the inverse-image submodule, the omitted surjectivity check and the compatibility of the lifted section.

proof.text: Write $p_k^L:L\to L_k$ for the quotient maps. An element of $I^kL$ is a finite sum $\sum_j a_jx_j$ with $a_j\in I^k$: the set of such sums is a submodule containing the given generators, and every such sum belongs to their generated submodule. Thus $v(I^kE)\subseteq I^kM$, and $v_k$ is well defined and $A_k$-linear. It is surjective: for $[m]\in M_k$ choose $e\in E$ with $v(e)=m$. Also $I^{k+1}L\subseteq I^kL$, since each product of $k+1$ elements of $I$ belongs to $I^k$. Hence the reductions are well defined, and $v_kq_k^E=q_k^Mv_{k+1}$ by evaluation on representatives.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, quotient maps preceding the induction.

proof.text: Fix $n\ge1$ and the prescribed section $s_n$. Define $P=(p_n^E)^{-1}(\operatorname{im}s_n)\subseteq E$. This is an $R$-submodule, since $s_n$ is $R$-linear after restriction of scalars and its image is closed under addition and scalar multiplication. It contains $I^nE$, whose reduction is zero. If $z\in P$, write $p_n^E(z)=s_n(b)$; applying $v_n$ and using $v_ns_n=\mathrm{id}$ gives $b=p_n^M(v(z))$. Consequently $p_n^E(z)=s_n(p_n^M(v(z)))$ for every $z\in P$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, definition of P_{n+1} and section identity.

proof.text: We check explicitly that $v|_P:P\to M$ is surjective. For $m\in M$, choose $z\in E$ representing $s_n(p_n^M(m))$. Then $z\in P$ and $m-v(z)\in I^nM$. Write $m-v(z)=\sum_{j=1}^r a_jm_j$ with $a_j\in I^n$, and choose $e_j\in E$ with $v(e_j)=m_j$. Put $h=\sum_j a_je_j\in I^nE\subseteq P$. Then $z+h\in P$ and $v(z+h)=v(z)+\sum_j a_jm_j=m$. This finite-sum calculation also covers the empty sum and uses neither flatness nor finite generation.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, the surjectivity assertion marked details omitted.

proof.text: Put $B=R/I^{n+1}$ and $T=P/I^{n+1}P$. Here $I^{n+1}P$ denotes the finite sums $\sum a_jz_j$ with $a_j\in I^{n+1}$ and $z_j\in P$. Define $\pi:T\to M_{n+1}$ and $j:T\to E_{n+1}$ by $\pi([z])=[v(z)]$ and $j([z])=[z]$. These are well defined: changing $z$ by such a sum changes its image by an element of $I^{n+1}M$ or $I^{n+1}E$, respectively. The formulas for addition and scalar multiplication show that both are $B$-linear; scalar lifts differing by an element of $I^{n+1}$ act identically on these quotients. By Step 3, $\pi$ is surjective. On representatives $v_{n+1}j=\pi$. No injectivity of $j$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, the maps from P_{n+1}/I^{n+1}P_{n+1}.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], maps out of a projective module lift along every module surjection. Apply this lifting property over $B$ to the surjection $\pi:T\to M_{n+1}$ of Step 4 and to $\mathrm{id}_{M_{n+1}}$. The hypothesis at level $n+1$ supplies projectivity over exactly $B$, so there is a $B$-linear $t:M_{n+1}\to T$ with $\pi t=\mathrm{id}$. Set $s_{n+1}=jt$. Then $s_{n+1}$ is $A_{n+1}$-linear and $v_{n+1}s_{n+1}=\pi t=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, choice of t; Tag 05CE, definition-projective, following paragraph (lifting formulation).

proof.text: For a representative $z\in P$, Step 2 gives $q_n^Ej([z])=p_n^E(z)=s_n(p_n^M(v(z)))=s_nq_n^M\pi([z])$. Thus $q_n^Ej=s_nq_n^M\pi$ as $R$-linear maps on $T$. Composing with $t$ gives $q_n^Es_{n+1}=s_nq_n^M\pi t=s_nq_n^M$, the required compatibility with the prescribed section. This argument uses representatives in $P$, not an identification of $T$ with a submodule of $E_{n+1}$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, final sentence: the composite works.

proof.text: For the family assertion, $v_1:E_1\to M_1$ is surjective by Step 1. The lifting clause of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], over $A_1$ and with the identity of the projective module $M_1$, gives a section $s_1$. For each positive $n$ and each section at level $n$, Steps 2--6 give at least one compatible section at level $n+1$. Choose one such successor for each pair $(n,s)$, and recurse on $n$ starting at $s_1$. The defining property of the successor yields $v_ns_n=\mathrm{id}$ and $q_n^Es_{n+1}=s_nq_n^M$ at each positive level. All compatibility equations are equations after restriction to $R$; no claim that maps between different quotient rings are linear over a single $A_n$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, induction starting with any splitting s_1; Tag 05CE lifting formulation.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, induction with the inverse-image submodule; the omitted surjectivity check and final compatibility are expanded explicitly. Tag 05CE supplies the stated projective lifting property.

lean.statement: theorem adic_projective_compatible_sections {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) {E : Type v} [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (v : E →ₗ[R] M) (hv : Function.Surjective v) (hprojective : ∀ n : ℕ, Module.Projective (R ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) (M ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • ⊤ : Submodule R M))) : (∀ (n : ℕ) (s : M ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • ⊤ : Submodule R M) →ₗ[R ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)] E ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • ⊤ : Submodule R E)), (v.reduceModIdeal (I ^ (n + 1))).comp s = LinearMap.id → ∃ t : M ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1 + 1) • ⊤ : Submodule R M) →ₗ[R ⧸ I ^ (n + 1 + 1)] E ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1 + 1) • ⊤ : Submodule R E), (v.reduceModIdeal (I ^ (n + 1 + 1))).comp t = LinearMap.id ∧ (Submodule.factorPowSucc I E (n + 1)).comp (t.restrictScalars R) = (s.restrictScalars R).comp (Submodule.factorPowSucc I M (n + 1))) ∧ (∃ s : (n : ℕ) → M ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • ⊤ : Submodule R M) →ₗ[R ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)] E ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • ⊤ : Submodule R E), ∀ n : ℕ, (v.reduceModIdeal (I ^ (n + 1))).comp (s n) = LinearMap.id ∧ (Submodule.factorPowSucc I E (n + 1)).comp ((s (n + 1)).restrictScalars R) = ((s n).restrictScalars R).comp (Submodule.factorPowSucc I M (n + 1)))
